subject: how to get the correlation-matrix with lavInspect at a manifest path-model

messages.author: 72ebbe9bcb85eab4
messages.subject: how to get the correlation-matrix with lavInspect at a manifest path-model
parts:
Dear all,

some years ago I could get the (empirical) correlation-matrix of the variables in my lavaan models with lavInspect(model, "sampstat") after having done the calculations (sem or cfa) using std.ov=TRUE. For some years now this still functions with CFA, but doesn't function anymore with manifest path-models: here, only the endogenous variables are standardized in the correlation/covariance-matrix I get with lavInspect. Because all manifest variables in a CFA are endogenous, I assume that this could be the reason, why I still get the full correlation-matrix at CFA-Models. (It seems to me that the behavior of lavInspect changed at the same time the optimizaion method NLMINB was introduced, but I'm not sure.)
Following the description of std.ov the calculations should be done using the correlation matrix of all observed variables, and there is no hint, that this is restricted to the endogenous variables of the model. So the question seems to be which informations are used by lavInspect.

Now the most important question for me is: Does there still exist a way to get the empirical correlation-matrix at (manifest) path models within lavaan?

Thanks for any answer and of course thanks for this package!

Edgar

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: how to get the correlation-matrix with lavInspect at a manifest path-model
parts:
On 5/5/20 2:03 PM, Edgar Schoreit wrote:
> Now the most important question for me is: Does there still exist a way
> to get the empirical correlation-matrix at (manifest) path models within
> lavaan?

My guess would be that you have exogenous variables in your model, and
by default, lavaan uses fixed.x = TRUE, implying that lavaan does not
'touch' your exogenous variables.

To get back your full correlation matrix, rerun the model with the
argument fixed.x = FALSE.

Yves.

messages.author: 72ebbe9bcb85eab4
messages.subject: Re: how to get the correlation-matrix with lavInspect at a manifest path-model
parts:
Oh yes, that's the reason. What a simple solution!
Thanks a lot!

Edgar
